title: Career Roadmap: System Administrator
summary: A System Administrator (SysAdmin) manages and maintains an organisation’s computer systems, servers, operating systems, user accounts, networks, backups, and security controls. This career suits students who enjoy troubleshooting, understanding how technology works, and keeping IT infrastructure reliable.

facts.Current degree: B.Sc. in Cloud Computing / Big Data Analytics

blocks.text: Recommended degree
B.Sc. in Cloud Computing, Big Data Analytics, Computer Science, or Information Technology.
Core focus
Operating systems, servers, networks, access management, cloud infrastructure, monitoring, and troubleshooting.
Potential workplaces
IT service providers, cloud service teams, data centres, SaaS companies, banks, universities, hospitals, and enterprise IT departments.
Key responsibilities

items.text: Install, configure, update, and maintain Windows and Linux systems.
Manage user accounts, permissions, and access policies.
Monitor server performance, uptime, storage, and resource usage.
Troubleshoot hardware, software, connectivity, and service failures.
Configure backups and test recovery procedures.
Apply security patches and follow security best practices.
Automate repetitive administration tasks using scripts.
Support cloud-based virtual machines, storage, and networking as responsibilities expand.

blocks.text: The following roadmap assumes a three-year B.Sc. programme. If the university offers a four-year honours or research track, use the additional year for advanced cloud engineering, internships, or a substantial capstone project.
Year 1 — Build the foundations
Fundamentals

items.text: Learn computer architecture, operating systems, programming fundamentals, and basic networking.
Practise Windows administration and introductory Linux commands.
Understand IP addresses, DNS, DHCP, ports, and network troubleshooting.
Learn Git and basic Python or Bash scripting.

blocks.label: Target outcome
blocks.text: Set up and troubleshoot a personal computer and a Linux virtual machine.
Year 2 — Practise system administration
Hands-on skills

items.text: Study Linux administration, Windows Server concepts, networking, and database fundamentals.
Practise users, groups, permissions, services, logs, storage, and scheduled tasks.
Learn virtualisation with VirtualBox or VMware Workstation.
Explore cloud virtual machines, identity and access management, monitoring, and backup tools.
Start documenting troubleshooting procedures.

blocks.label: Target outcome
blocks.text: Build and maintain a small multi-machine lab.
Year 3 — Specialise and become job-ready
Career preparation

blocks.label: Choose a primary platform
blocks.text: Linux administration, Windows administration, or cloud infrastructure.

items.text: Learn shell scripting, Python automation, infrastructure monitoring, and incident response.
Practise backup restoration, patch management, access reviews, and disaster recovery.
Complete an internship or a realistic infrastructure project.
Prepare a portfolio, resume, and practical troubleshooting demonstrations.

blocks.label: Target outcome
blocks.text: Apply for Junior System Administrator, IT Support Engineer, or Infrastructure Support roles.

TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, subnetting, routing, firewalls, VPNs

AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud fundamentals

blocks.text: Build practical projects that demonstrate your ability to configure, monitor, and recover systems.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Linux server administration lab
Install Linux in a virtual machine, create users and groups, configure file permissions, manage services, inspect logs, and schedule routine tasks.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: setup guide, command reference, troubleshooting log, and screenshots.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Cloud virtual machine deployment
Deploy a small virtual machine on a cloud provider, configure restricted access, enable monitoring, and document its cost and security settings.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: architecture diagram, configuration notes, access rules, and cost estimate.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Server monitoring and alerting
Track CPU, memory, disk usage, and availability. Configure alerts for simulated resource exhaustion or service failures.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: monitoring dashboard, alert rules, sample incident report, and resolution steps.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Automated backup and recovery
Write a Bash or PowerShell script to back up selected files, record failures, and verify restoration in a test environment.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: source code, backup schedule, recovery test results, and a short disaster recovery plan.
Search for these job titles while studying or after graduation:

Desktop Support Engineer

blocks.text: A direct System Administrator role may require practical experience. IT support or infrastructure support can be a useful first step toward server and cloud administration.

rows.text: Windows, Azure, identity, and infrastructure fundamentals

blocks.text: Certifications worth considering, depending on your chosen path:

blocks.label: Linux
blocks.text: Linux Professional Institute Linux Essentials, followed by LPIC-1 when ready.

blocks.label: Networking
blocks.text: Cisco CCNA, particularly for network-heavy infrastructure roles.

blocks.label: Cloud
blocks.text: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner or Microsoft Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900).

blocks.label: System administration
blocks.text: Microsoft Windows Server learning paths and relevant role-based training.
Certification names, exam availability, and syllabi can change; verify details on the official provider websites. Certifications complement practical projects rather than replacing them.
After your B.Sc., consider these routes based on your interests and eligibility:

items.text: M.Sc. Computer Science / Information Technology: Broader computing and infrastructure foundations.

blocks.label: M.Sc. Cloud Computing
blocks.text: Specialisation in cloud platforms, virtualisation, and infrastructure.

blocks.label: MCA
blocks.text: A broader software and computing route, subject to university admission requirements.

items.text: M.Sc. Data Science / Big Data Analytics: More suitable if you want to move toward data engineering or analytics rather than traditional system administration.

blocks.text: A postgraduate degree is not normally essential for every entry-level system administration role. Practical experience and demonstrated technical skills are often important.

blocks.label: Stage 1
blocks.text: IT Support / Infrastructure Support
Troubleshoot user issues, devices, access, and basic systems.

blocks.label: Stage 2
blocks.text: System Administrator
Own server maintenance, user administration, monitoring, backups, and patching.

blocks.label: Stage 3
blocks.text: Senior SysAdmin / Cloud Administrator
Manage complex environments, automate operations, and improve reliability.

blocks.label: Stage 4
blocks.text: Infrastructure Engineer / Cloud Engineer / SRE
Design resilient systems, automate infrastructure, and lead reliability improvements.
Progression depends on experience, technical depth, and the responsibilities of each role; it is not tied to a fixed timeline.

blocks.label: Infrastructure as Code
blocks.text: Terraform and Ansible for repeatable system configuration.

blocks.label: Containers
blocks.text: Docker and Kubernetes fundamentals.

blocks.label: Cloud operations
blocks.text: Cloud monitoring, identity management, and cost optimisation.

blocks.label: Cybersecurity
blocks.text: Zero-trust principles, vulnerability management, and security monitoring.

blocks.label: AI-assisted IT operations
blocks.text: Using anomaly detection and automated incident analysis to support troubleshooting.

blocks.label: Site Reliability Engineering (SRE)
blocks.text: Availability, incident response, service-level objectives, and automation.

Recommended target profile

By graduation, aim to have a working knowledge of Linux, networking, Windows administration, basic scripting, cloud fundamentals, monitoring, and backup recovery, supported by at least three documented practical projects.
The strongest initial target is Junior System Administrator or Infrastructure Support Engineer, with a planned progression into cloud administration or infrastructure engineering.
